title: Learning Compatible Multi-Prize Subnetworks for Asymmetric Retrieval

Learning Compatible Multi-Prize Subnetworks for Asymmetric Retrieval
Yushuai Sun1*, Zikun Zhou2*†, Dongmei Jiang2, Yaowei Wang2,
Jun Yu1, Guangming Lu1, and Wenjie Pei1,2†
1Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen
2Pengcheng Laboratory
Abstract
Asymmetric retrieval is a typical scenario in real-world
retrieval systems, where compatible models of varying
capacities are deployed on platforms with different re-
source conﬁgurations.
Existing methods generally train
pre-deﬁned networks or subnetworks with capacities specif-
ically designed for pre-determined platforms, using com-
patible learning.
